question: The Supreme Court extended the stay on tree cutting in how many acres of land at Kancha Gachibowli in Hyderabad in April 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**400 acres**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Supreme Court of India**, in **April 2025**, issued an extension on the stay order regarding the cutting of trees in the **Kancha Gachibowli** region of **Hyderabad**.
 
• The specific area protected under this judicial intervention covers **400 acres** of land, which is considered a vital ecological zone in the city.
 
• The court's decision was prompted by the need to evaluate the environmental impact of proposed developmental projects on this **400-acre** stretch, which houses a significant number of heritage trees and local flora.
 
• This legal stay prevents the **Telangana Government** or any private contractors from proceeding with land clearing activities that could lead to large-scale deforestation in the **IT corridor**.
 
• Environmental activists had filed petitions highlighting that the destruction of this greenery would violate existing **environmental norms** and exacerbate the urban heat island effect in **Hyderabad**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kancha Gachibowli:** This area is located in the **Serilingampally mandal** of **Hyderabad**. It has been a subject of long-standing litigation involving land ownership disputes and **environmental conservation** efforts.
 
• **Biodiversity Value:** The **400 acres** in question serve as a "green lung" for the rapidly urbanizing parts of western **Hyderabad**, providing a habitat for various species of birds and small fauna.
 
• **Legal Context:** The **Supreme Court** often intervenes in such matters under the **Public Trust Doctrine**, which mandates that the state must protect natural resources for the enjoyment of the general public rather than permitting their conversion into private ownership or commercial use.
 
• **Urban Development vs. Nature:** The conflict in **Gachibowli** reflects a broader national challenge in **India** where infrastructure expansion frequently clashes with the preservation of **urban forests** and catchment areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Article 21:** The **Judiciary** frequently links the protection of the environment to **Article 21** of the **Constitution of India**, which guarantees the **Right to Life**, including the right to a healthy environment.
 
• **Forest (Conservation) Act:** Any diversion of land that qualifies as a forest or contains a high density of trees typically requires clearance under the **Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980**.
 
• **Historical Precedents:** This case draws parallels to other major environmental litigations in **India**, such as the **Aarey Forest** case in **Mumbai**, where the **Supreme Court** had to balance transit infrastructure needs with **forest preservation**.
 
• **Impact of April 2025 Ruling:** The extension of the stay on these **400 acres** ensures that no irreversible environmental damage occurs while the court examines the **Detailed Project Reports (DPR)** and environmental clearance certificates.
